name: AMBROSIA
description: Practical semantic parsers are expected to understand user utterances and map them to executable programs, even when these are ambiguous. We introduce a new benchmark, AMBROSIA, which we hope will inform and inspire the development of text-to-SQL parsers capable of recognizing and interpreting ambiguous requests. Our dataset contains questions showcasing three different types of ambiguity (scope ambiguity, attachment ambiguity, and vagueness), their interpretations, and corresponding SQL queries. In each case, the ambiguity persists even when the database context is provided. This is achieved through a novel approach that involves controlled generation of databases from scratch. We benchmark various LLMs on AMBROSIA, revealing that even the most advanced models struggle to identify and interpret ambiguity in questions.
evaluation_method: exact_match (SQL string match) and execution-based accuracy (whether produced SQL yields correct results on database)
typical_sota_score: unknown (reported results indicate even strong LLMs struggle substantially on ambiguity recognition)
reputation: New (2024) targeted benchmark focused on linguistic ambiguity in text-to-SQL; of growing interest for semantic-parsing researchers but not yet widely adopted.
notes: Specialized dataset emphasizing ambiguous queries; evaluation requires generated SQL execution on synthetic databases; not saturated and small-to-moderate in scale; potential overlap risk if models were pre-trained on similar text-to-SQL corpora.
